text:
mike: heads up — we had a cluster-level spike in preemptible evictions in us-west2 around 07:12UTC, and several streaming requests dropped during token/model cutover. logs show `stream_cutover: timeout` and a handful of 503s from the runtime

anya: saw the alert. most of the failed streams were long-running chats (~1.5k-2k tokens) — client disconnected mid-cutover.

hana: timeline? was there a graceful drain or immediate preempt?

mike: GCP sent the preempt notice, our drain sequence started but the runtime tried to do a token/model switch in the same window and we lost the socket. looks like the swap wasn't atomic w.r.t. streaming consumer.

jules: thinking out loud: we need a small handshake between node runtime and router for token cutover + a short requeue window on disconnect. This avoids forcing clients to reconnect across model variants.

sre-oncall: we should also preserve prefix/KV cache pointers when we requeue; otherwise requeueing causes a cold cache miss and extra tokens/cost.

anya: agree. proposal sketch:
```
# cutover handshake (pseudo)
1) node receives PREEMPT_NOTICE (t + 30s)
2) node enters DRAIN_READ_ONLY (stop accepting new requests for that node)
3) node sends CUTOVER_PREPARE(token_id, model_version) -> router
4) router validates and replies PREPARE_ACK (or REJECT)
5) on PREPARE_ACK node swaps active token atomically and marks STREAM_HANDOVER_READY
6) router routes *existing* streams to STREAM_HANDOVER_READY node for up to requeue_window seconds
7) if client disconnects during window -> router requeues to any compatible node preserving prefix pointers
```

jules: config knobs we discussed in the past, but tweaked:
```
cutover:
  handshake_timeout: 8s   # time router waits for PREPARE_ACK
  requeue_window: 12s    # how long we accept requeued streams after disconnect
  preserve_kv_prefix: true
  fail_open_after: 20s    # if handshake fails, fallback to best-effort routing
```

hana: +1 to handshake_timeout being small. if handshake takes too long we increase latency and block other nodes. 8s seems reasonable given network RTTs.

sre-oncall: metric requirements: count(cutover_start), count(cutover_ack), count(requeues), hist(latency_add_per_requeue), gauge(active_cutovers). need alerts if requeues > 0.5% of streaming traffic in a 5m window.

mike: also add cost/quality signal: token-bloat per requeue (additional tokens sent after requeue) — we saw a few cases where requeue produced duplicate prefixes.

anya: questions: 1) do we requeue to the same model version only, or allow compatible downgraded variant? 2) how do we handle auth token rotation if token id changed during swap?

jules: prefer same model_version first; fallback to compatible quantized variant only if canary indicates equivalence. for auth tokens: handshake must include token fingerprint, router can reissue ephemeral stream token for the requeue target.

mike: we need an integration test that simulates preempt notice midstream, and asserts no more than X% client disconnects and median added latency < 120ms. hana can run load test on canary with 1k concurrent streaming connections and 20% spot nodes.

hana: I'll build the k6 scenario and a small simulator that sends PREEMPT_NOTICE to nodes. assigning: @jules for router handshake impl, @anya for runtime changes (atomic swap), @mike for metrics/dashboards.

infra-bot: scheduled deploy cutover-handshake v0.1 to canary at 02:00 UTC tomorrow (canary: 5% traffic). Reaction: :rocket:

anya: one more safety: add a per-request idempotency token so requeued requests can resume without double-processing user-visible actions. lightweight UUID in request metadata.

jules: will add idempotency field and preserve during requeue. also will add a small exponential backoff client header so clients know to retry once within requeue window.

mike: sounds good. let's land canary, run the HA load tests, and watch the new metrics. if requeues spike or token-bloat > 0.1 tokens/requeue we'll rollback. :thumbsup:
